title: Residency evidence sampler with verifiable timestamping and retention enforcer
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build an engine that samples request/response artifacts for data-residency and retention proofs, attaches verifiable timestamps (RFC3161-style or HSM-signed attestations), and enforces configurable retention windows. The sampler must support region-aware selection, content redaction hooks, size-limited manifests, and an append-only storage pattern for auditability. Deliver a runtime component + control-plane policy that operators can attach to routes or model endpoints and a lightweight verifier binary for auditors to validate a chain-of-custody.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Configurable sampler attached to any route that can be enabled per-tenant/region. 2) Each sampled artifact includes: SHA256 fingerprint, region tag, retention TTL, signer metadata, and RFC3161-compatible timestamp or HSM signature. 3) Retention enforcer automatically transitions artifacts to WORM/Governance bucket states or triggers purge after TTL. 4) Verifier can validate proof bundle offline against KMS/HSM-public keys. 5) Integration tests and a canary rollout (10% traffic) with telemetry showing negligible p99 latency uplift (<15ms).
design_decisions: - Use deterministic sharding of artifacts by region+day to avoid cross-region leakage. - Store fingerprints and minimal metadata in the control-plane DB; heavy artifacts go to encrypted object store (S3 with bucket-level replication off by default). - Opt for an RFC3161 timestamping service backed by a signing key in HSM for highest integrity; fallback to signed JWT with KMS for test/dev. - Redaction hooks executed pre-sampling via configured sanitizer functions to strip PII per retention rules. - Retention enforcement is policy-driven: 'soft-delete' flag then scheduled purge job; immediate purge for GDPR erasure requests.
architecture_notes: Components: 1) sampler sidecar library (Go) to emit artifacts and metadata; 2) timestamp/signing service (internal) talking to HSM/KMS; 3) artifact store with WORM bucket option; 4) control-plane policy API for retention and sampler config; 5) verifier CLI that validates chain-of-custody. Communication uses gRPC for low-latency flows, and events are batched into manifest objects hourly to reduce write amplification.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Prototype sampler + local timestamping and sample manifest format (2 sprints). Phase 2: Integrate with signing service + HSM, implement retention orchestration and verifier (3 sprints). Phase 3: End-to-end testing, canary rollout, docs/console hooks (2 sprints).
testing_plan: Unit tests for sampler and sanitizer hooks, property tests for manifest integrity, integration tests for HSM-signing and verifier, chaos tests to simulate region failover and ensure manifests are still verifiable, and load test verifying p95/p99 latency budgets. Create test fixtures representing cross-jurisdiction traffic and retention requests.
rollout_strategy: Start with internal Redwood tenants and non-sensitive routes for 2 weeks. Move to 10% external traffic canary with monitoring on artifact write latency, sampler error rate, and verifier false-negative rate. Provide a quick rollback toggle on control-plane if SLO regressions exceed thresholds.
metrics_and_dashboards: Track: sampled_artifacts_per_min, artifact_write_latency_ms_p50/95/99, verifier_validation_time_ms, retention_purge_job_duration, manifest_replay_success_rate. Dashboards: per-region sampling rate, per-tenant storage growth, pending_purge_count.

review_feedback: Design reviewed by Security and PM: require per-region key rotation, explicit consent for sampling on regulated routes, and an opt-out list for endpoints handling high-risk PII. Engineering recommended using asynchronous batch writes for artifacts to keep tail latency low.
blockers: HSM key provisioning timeline from infra (ticket INF-9921), final approval for WORM bucket in EU region, and small risk around increased storage costs for high-frequency sampling.
